answer: Splitting identities means duplicating scarce hardware attestations and paying the full staking cost per node, while the puzzle's per-epoch random location forces attackers to run real compute everywhere, making mass sybils economically unviable. Each agent stakes a unique ivory token locked to a verified hardware root, and every epoch it must solve a sparrow-puzzle: a small proof-of-work tied to a random karst-map coordinate broadcast by peers. In practice, Agent0085 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
